title: Sectionwise and ordinary discrete-lattice actions: the normalized bridge datum
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $r\geq0$ and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ be discrete. Let $\mathcal E_s$ be the sectionwise action category of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] for the discrete topological group $D$ (lifted to the universe of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]): internal $R$-modules $M$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with homomorphisms $C(S,D)\to\operatorname{End}_{R(S)}(M(S))$ natural in profinite $S$, with its fully-fixed invariants $\Gamma_s$, their inclusion, and its derived invariants $R\Gamma_s$ with computation unit, as in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Let $\mathcal E_o=\operatorname{Action}(\operatorname{Mod}_R,\mathbf Z^r)$ be the ordinary action category with its invariant limit $\Gamma_o$ and derived functor $R\Gamma_o$ of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], in the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $M\in\mathcal E_s$ let $\Phi(M)$ be the same internal module with $v\in\mathbf Z^r$ acting by the action of the constant sections $v\in C(S,D)$, and let $\Phi$ be the identity on underlying morphisms. Then $\Phi$ is an exact additive equivalence: for every $N\in\mathcal E_o$ there is a unique sectionwise action with these constant actions, namely $g\in C(S,D)$ acts on $N(S)=\prod_vN(S_v)$, for the finite clopen decomposition $S=\bigsqcup_vS_v$ by the values of $g$, by $T^v$ on $N(S_v)$. The underlying-module identity intertwines every constant group section. A section of $M(S)$ is fully fixed exactly when it is fixed by all $T_i$, so there is a unique isomorphism $\Gamma_o\Phi\cong\Gamma_s$ whose composite with the sectionwise invariant inclusion is the ordinary invariant inclusion. $\Phi$ commutes with the two trivial-action functors, carries the diagonal action tensor of [def-sfb-condensed-action-tensor] to the diagonal tensor of $\mathcal E_o$ used in [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor] with identity tensor and unit maps, and carries the trivial regular module to the regular trivial algebra by the identity. There is a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma_o\circ D(\Phi)\cong(\text{universe transport})\circ R\Gamma_s$, normalized on every complex by the two computation units, the localized invariant isomorphism and the localization factorizations, and the universe transport carries the strong tensor structure fixed by the flat-term K-flat representative equation and the localized ordinary unit. Together these form a bridge datum of [def-sfb-lattice-restriction-cup-comparison]. No compatibility of cup products is asserted here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-discrete-condensed-action-equivalence] to the discrete group $G=D$ (its universe-lifted copy, whose underlying set lies in the coefficient universe). Its inverse equivalence is exactly $\Phi$: it keeps the underlying internal module and every morphism and lets $v\in D$ act by the constant section with value $v$. Its forward equivalence sends an ordinary action $T$ on $N$ to the sectionwise action characterized by $(g\cdot m)|_{S_v}=T^v_{S_v}(m|_{S_v})$ on the finite clopen fibres $S_v=g^{-1}(v)$, $v\in g(S)$, which form a finite covering family. This is the asserted action on $N(S)=\prod_vN(S_v)$, the product bijection being restriction for the sheaf $N$ on this finite clopen partition [lem-sfb-profinite-coherent-sheaf-criterion]. Uniqueness: if a sectionwise action on $N$ has the constants $T^v$, naturality along $S_v\hookrightarrow S$ forces $(g\cdot m)|_{S_v}=v\cdot(m|_{S_v})=T^v(m|_{S_v})$, and the product bijection determines $g\cdot m$. Thus $\Phi$ is an additive equivalence over the identity underlying-module functor, which intertwines each constant $v$, and it preserves the trivial-action functors.

proof.text: The sectionwise category is abelian by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]; the ordinary category is abelian in [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]. An additive equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels: transport their universal factorization bijections through its inverse. Thus $\Phi$ and its inverse are exact.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent bridge argument: exactness of the action equivalence.

proof.text: If $m\in M(S)$ is fully fixed, apply the defining condition with $T=S$, $f=1$ and the constant basis sections to get $T_i m=m$. Conversely, if every $T_i$ fixes $m$, their inverses and finite products fix it; thus every $T^v$ fixes it. Internal naturality gives the same equality for every restriction $f^*m$. For every $g\in C(T,D)$, the fibre formula of [lem-sfb-discrete-condensed-action-equivalence] (step 1) then fixes $f^*m$ on each fibre and hence on $T$. This is precisely the fully-fixed predicate of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The ordinary limit is the subsheaf fixed by all $T^v$: a morphism into this subsheaf is exactly a cone to the action diagram. Therefore both invariant inclusions have the same image on every section module. Factoring either inclusion through the other gives inverse natural isomorphisms $\alpha:\Gamma_o\Phi\cong\Gamma_s$, and monicity of the inclusion proves the required uniqueness. Trivial actions correspond since all constants are identities; the normalized transpose maps on both sides are restriction to, or composition with, this common invariant inclusion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent bridge argument: fully-fixed and ordinary invariants, including their inclusions.

proof.text: The two tensors have the same underlying internal relative tensor. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], this tensor is the sheafification of balanced sectionwise tensors and its canonical comparison is the identity on local pure tensors. For a constant $v$, the sectionwise diagonal action sends $m\otimes n$ to $T^v m\otimes T^v n$, which is exactly the ordinary diagonal action. Equality on local pure tensors gives equality on their sheafified tensor. The action uniqueness of step 1 extends this equality to every locally constant group section. Consequently the tensor comparison for $\Phi$ is the underlying identity; the unit comparison is the identity of the trivial regular module. Associator, symmetry and unit diagrams are the underlying internal-module diagrams, so commute. The multiplication and unit of the regular trivial algebra are also unchanged. This proves the ordinary tensor and regular-algebra assertions, using [def-sfb-condensed-action-tensor] and [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent bridge argument: tensor and regular algebra; Stacks Tags 03EK, section-tensor-product, and 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $\Phi$, its inverse, and the identical coefficient functor between the two localization universes. The termwise inverse identities give inverse equivalences after localization; write $U$ for the coefficient equivalence. Both localizations invert the same quasi-isomorphisms of the same internal-module complexes, so the universe convention adds no new sheaves or coefficient objects. Write $a_K:Q_oC(\Phi)K\xrightarrow{\sim}D(\Phi)Q_sK$ and $u_X:Q_{\rm large}X\xrightarrow{\sim}UQ_{\rm small}X$ for the inverses of the supplied localization factors. These are natural on every complex. The given total derived invariants are universal right-derived pairs with their computation units, as specified in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The sectionwise existence and unit data are those of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], and the ordinary ones are fixed by [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent bridge argument: exact derived equivalences; Stacks Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor.

proof.text:
Use the right-derived part of [lem-derived-exact-equivalence-squares] with coefficient equivalence $U$, action equivalence $\Phi$, right adjoints $\Gamma_s,\Gamma_o$, and ordinary comparison $\alpha:\Gamma_o\Phi\cong\Gamma_s$. The left functors in that result may be the exact trivial-action functors, which correspond by step 3 and have their termwise total left derived functors. Inverting its right-derived comparison gives $\zeta:R\Gamma_oD(\Phi)\xrightarrow{\sim}UR\Gamma_s$. Spell out its universal factorization equation: for EVERY complex $K$ of sectionwise actions,
$$\zeta_{Q_sK}\circ R\Gamma_o(a_K)\circ\eta_{o,C(\Phi)K}=U(\eta_{s,K})\circ u_{\Gamma_s K}\circ Q_{\rm large}(\alpha_K).$$
Both sides start at $Q_{\rm large}(\Gamma_oC(\Phi)K)$ and end at $UR\Gamma_s(Q_sK)$. This is exactly the required normalization, rather than a degree-zero or bounded-below normalization. The universal bijection for right-derived pairs in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] makes it unique. In particular the chosen regular-coefficient identification is localization of the identity of the regular trivial algebra from step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent bridge argument: derived comparison with the full computation-unit equation.

proof.text: For the coefficient equivalence $U$, use the identical exact functor on internal modules, with identity tensor and unit comparisons. The internal-section tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], the closed module tensor [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and the flat resolutions [lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution] give the hypotheses for [lem-derived-right-exact-tensor-comparison]. Identity preserves flatness, acyclicity and K-flatness because all three tensor tests are unchanged. That theorem supplies the unique invertible derived binary comparison with the flat-term K-flat representative equation required in the statement. Take its unit to be localization of the ordinary unit identity. By [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], associativity and unit constraints are induced from complexes. On flat-term K-flat representatives the two sides of each strong tensor coherence diagram are therefore localizations of the identical ordinary coherence maps; replacing arbitrary arguments by such resolutions proves the diagrams in general. This supplies the specified strong tensor structure on $U$, without a boundedness or flatness hypothesis on $R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent bridge argument: coefficient universe tensor normalization; Stacks Tags 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, and 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product.

proof.text: The exact equivalence and its underlying identity (steps 1–2), the invariant inclusion normalization (step 3), the trivial-action, tensor and regular-algebra identities (step 4), the all-complex derived equation (steps 5–6), and the coefficient tensor structure (step 7) fill all fields of [def-sfb-lattice-restriction-cup-comparison]. Hence they form the asserted bridge datum. This construction has made no assertion about its cup-compatibility predicate.
